page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-192 is an x86_64 architecture server instance characterized by its high memory-to-core allocation. The system supplies 192 dedicated vCPUs combined with 1512 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include integrated graphics processing units and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The instance provides no bundled local storage volumes. Workloads deployed on this type must utilize network-attached or cloud-managed external storage for persistent filesystems. This decouples compute scaling from disk provisioning, though storage latency depends strictly on remote storage attachment interfaces. Dedicated CPU core assignment ensures processing threads operate without neighbor contention common to shared-core or burstable configurations.

From a resource utilization standpoint, concentrating 192 cores and 1512 GB of memory in a single operating boundary offers cost efficiency for monolithic deployments that would otherwise require managing multiple distributed instances. The hardware profile is appropriate for enterprise in-memory databases, large caching layers, batch ETL processing, large transactional data engines, and data science workloads requiring expansive RAM working sets.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-192 is an x86_64 compute instance designed for large memory footprints, offering 192 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1512 GB of system memory. This configuration provides approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, aligning with memory-intensive compute requirements. The instance features dedicated CPU allocation without hardware GPU accelerators. Local storage is not included, requiring external disk configurations for persistent data storage. With its heavy memory allocation and high physical compute capacity, this server delivers qualitative resource efficiency for centralized enterprise infrastructure that demands extensive RAM without the physical footprint of multiple smaller hosts. Because all storage must be provisioned independently, architecture planning must account for external storage volume performance. The server is suited for massive in-memory databases, large-scale caching clusters, extract-transform-load pipelines, and data-intensive enterprise workloads.
